stories.title: Nepal-Tibet floods: At least 11 Malaysians missing
stories.summary: At least 11 Malaysians are missing after severe floods hit Nepal’s Rasuwa district, causing over 160 deaths and widespread destruction. Malaysia’s embassy in Kathmandu is coordinating with local authorities and rescue teams to locate the missing Malaysians and ensure their safety. Malaysians in Nepal are advised to stay vigilant, avoid risky areas, update contact details via e-Konsular, and follow local safety instructions. About a dozen Malaysians are among hundreds of people still missing after massive floods hit Nepal’s Rasuwa district, destroying villages and leaving at least 160 dead. Malaysia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said that it had received reports from the embassy in Kathmandu that contact had been lost with 11 Malaysians believed to be in the badly-affected Rasuwa district, near the Nepal-China border. Nepali authorities, however, said 17 Malaysians were among more than 300 foreigners reported missing from the affected areas. Houses, cars and buildings have been swept away in a deluge of water after an avalanche further in the snowy-mountains triggered massive floods in the valley. The swollen river also caused widespread damage to roads, bridges, electricity and communication infrastructure in affected areas, causing loss of contact with Malaysians there, said the ministry. “The embassy is actively coordinating with local authorities and the search and rescue teams currently being deployed by the Nepalese government to locate the affected Malaysians and ascertain their safety,” the ministry said in a statement. It advised Malaysians living in or travelling through Nepal, particularly those near the affected areas, to remain vigilant, prioritise their safety and comply with instructions from local authorities. They are also urged to register and update their contact details through the e-Konsular portal at https://ekonsular.kln.gov.my to enable timely communication and consular assistance. For immediate consular assistance or emergencies, Malaysian citizens are urged to contact the Embassy directly via its emergency helpline at +977-980-100-8000 or email mwkathmandu@kln.gov.my.

stories.title: Nepal-Tibet floods: At least 9 South Koreans missing, 10 others confirmed safe
stories.summary: At least nine South Korean workers were missing and 10 others were evacuated after sudden flooding struck Nepal’s Rasuwa region in the morning on Aug 26, according to Seoul’s Foreign Ministry. The nine missing workers are employees of the Korea South-East Power and Doosan Enerbility who had been working at a hydroelectric power plant construction site in the area. The ministry had initially said eight Koreans were unaccounted for, but the South Korean Embassy in Kathmandu later confirmed with Doosan Enerbility that one additional employee could not be reached. Nepali authorities dispatched a rescue team consisting of military and police personnel to the affected area and are carrying out search and rescue operations, the ministry said. Another 10 South Korean employees of Doosan Enerbility were initially reported as being stranded at the site awaiting rescue, though the company confirmed they were safe. The Foreign Minister later confirmed that the 10 employees were evacuated to safety with other Nepali and foreign workers. They are accompanied by a Korean consul dispatched to the area, according to the ministry. Doosan Enerbility, which is carrying out engineering, procurement and construction work for the hydropower project, said it had immediately set up an emergency response headquarters and planned to dispatch a team early on Aug 27, including CEO Jung Yeon-in, to Nepal. Korea South-East Power also said three of its employees at the site could not be reached. The state-run power company said it had set up an emergency situation room and plans to dispatch a response team to Nepal on Aug 27. South Korea’s embassy in Nepal also notified authorities there immediately after learning of the incident and requested swift search and rescue efforts for the eight missing nationals. A consular official was also dispatched to the scene.

stories.title: China launches world’s first 100kW bamboo-built floating solar farm off Shandong coast
stories.summary: China has launched the world’s first 100-kilowatt (kW) floating solar farm built with bamboo frames, offering a more environmentally friendly approach to offshore energy. The floating solar platform, named Jilin-2, is made of composite bamboo tubes and pipes. It has been deployed at a demonstration base off the coast of Yantai in the eastern province of Shandong. It will supply power to an integrated hydrogen, ammonia and methanol production project, manufacturer Yantai CIMC Raffles Ocean...

stories.title: BOK lifts S. Korea's growth outlook to 3.3 pct for 2026 on strong chip exports
stories.summary: The Bank of Korea (BOK) on Thursday raised its economic growth forecast for South Korea to 3.3 percent for this year, citing strong semiconductor exports driven by steady demand for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure. The revision represents a 0.7 percentage-point increase from the BOK's previous forecast of 2.6 percent issued in May. The central bank has raised its 2026 growth forecast two times since it projected 2 percent growth in February. For 2027, the central bank estimated its growth outlook at 2.9 percent, up from 2.1 percent in May. The South Korean economy grew 1.8 percent in the first quarter from a quarter earlier, marking the strongest quarterly growth since the third quarter of 2020, when the economy expanded 2.2 percent. In the second quarter, Asia's fourth-largest economy expanded 0.6 percent, sharply exceeding the BOK's May forecast of 0.2 percent growth. Against this backdrop, the government last month predicted the economy will grow 3 percent in 2026.
